findings.summary: The new sentence 'The same trigger set is the ArrTags-side provider inventory cache invalidation set' is imprecise because the preceding refresh-trigger list includes Jellyfin ItemAdded/ItemUpdated/ItemRemoved events, which are not wired to invalidate the inventory cache.
findings.detail: docs/architecture.md section 8 lists refresh triggers as (1) Jellyfin ItemAdded/relevant ItemUpdated/ItemRemoved events, (2) post-scan, (3) manual/periodic scheduled, (4) webhooks. The worker added 'The same trigger set is the ArrTags-side provider inventory cache invalidation set (ADR-018 clause 3): an accepted webhook invalidates its connection, and a reconciliation (post-scan, manual/periodic scheduled, or post-save) invalidates the retained observation sets...'. Per ADR-018 clause 3 the complete invalidation set is webhook, Jellyfin library refresh/post-scan, scheduled/manual reconciliation, and the bounded TTL fallback (the ADR's own 'complete trigger set' sentence enumerates webhook, post-scan, manual, TTL and does not include per-item Jellyfin events). The implementation wires webhook + post-scan + scheduled/manual + post-save + TTL, which matches the ADR. Per-item Jellyfin library events (src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsLifecycleService.OnLibraryItemChanged) enqueue work hints directly and do not invalidate; that is consistent with the ADR, but the 'same trigger set' wording could be read as claiming they do. This is a wording precision issue only; the functional invalidation set is correct.
findings.recommended_action: Optionally clarify in the task 11.4 documentation pass that the invalidation set is webhook + library refresh/post-scan + scheduled/manual reconciliation + bounded TTL (and post-save), and that per-item Jellyfin library events do not invalidate the provider inventory cache.

findings.summary: The 'no revision token / history-since' negative test excludes two literal markers but does not pin the allowed provider endpoint set, so a differently named revision/history fetch would not be caught.
findings.detail: ProviderReadsUseNoConditionalRequestRevisionTokenOrHistorySinceWatermark asserts the absence of If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since/If-Match and of the literal substrings 'history/since' and 'h=' on the captured URIs. Source inspection independently confirms the shipped reads issue only the documented library and bulk-selection endpoints and add no revision/history/conditional mechanism, so the acceptance criterion is met by the implementation; this is a coverage-completeness observation, not a live defect. This corroborates the separate test-quality review (docs/implementation/11.3/test-quality-review.json, TQ-11.3-1, MEDIUM, open).
evidence: grep of changed source for If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since/history/since/SignalR -> only a doc comment in ArrInventoryCache.cs
findings.recommended_action: Optional: assert every captured request path is in the documented provider endpoint set. Not required to satisfy the 11.3 acceptance criteria.

findings.summary: The documented in-flight single-flight population race is real, honestly stated, and its bounded consequence is acceptable for a non-authoritative accelerator.
findings.detail: ArrInventoryCacheProvider.Invalidate/InvalidateAll do not acquire the per-connection population gate, so a population that started before an invalidation and completes after it can store the provider read it took before the invalidation (reader: Radarr/SonarrMetadataReader reads cache -> acquires gate -> re-checks -> reads provider -> TryStore). The stored pre-invalidation set can then be served until its configured TTL (OperationalLimits.InventoryCacheTtlMinutes default 15, validated range 1-1440) or the next invalidation. The cache is explicitly non-authoritative and the consequence is bounded and repaired; ADR-018 does not require single-flight coalescing or a generation counter, and the task asked for this behavior to be documented rather than fenced. The worker documents it in the cache XML docs, PLANS.md 11.3, docs/architecture.md section 8, docs/data-model.md section 6, docs/changelog.md, and the worker report, and does not overstate the guarantee.
findings.recommended_action: No action; keep the bounded consequence documented as-is.
